sections.h2: What does the City of San Angelo charge per $100?
sections.html:
The city's budget page shows a rate of $0.7947 per $100 of valuation. It appears alongside the adopted budget for fiscal year 2026 to 2027 and a link to the Tom Green County Appraisal District's tool for breaking down a local bill.

The city is one layer of the total. Other units on the parcel add their own, and the combined figure is your bill. The same page prints sales tax pieces that add to 8.25 percent with the state's 6.25 percent, and a city hotel occupancy rate of 7 percent.

The budget office is in City Hall at 72 W. College Ave., and the page links a Taxpayer Impact Statement.

sections.h2: Where do I pay or contest San Angelo property tax?
sections.html:
San Angelo lies in Tom Green County, and two offices matter: the Tom Green Central Appraisal District at 2302 Pulliam, and the county's Tax Assessor-Collector office at 113 West Beauregard, which lists main-office hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

For online payment, the district's instructions are to open your account, select the Tax Summary tab and follow the pay link shown when a balance is due. E-check and cards are accepted. The district's site also has a tax estimator and a page on the protest process.

  • The district named May 15 as the protest deadline for many residential properties, and accepted protests by email, mail, drop-off or its website.
  • The deadline for your own parcel is printed on your Notice of Appraised Value.
  • Drop boxes take payments and documents.

sections.h2: What if the review board keeps my San Angelo value?
sections.html: Three routes remain: a lawsuit in district court, binding arbitration, or a hearing at the State Office of Administrative Hearings, which takes values over $1,000,000. Whichever you pick, send the undisputed tax by the delinquency date. Keep every notice, and photograph condition problems, since those records carry weight.

sections.h2: What late charges can a San Angelo bill pick up?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in October and are due by January 31 in most cases. The first day of delinquency is February 1, when a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest are charged.

The penalty climbs a point monthly until it is 12 percent on July 1, and interest keeps building at 1 percent a month. An attorney hired by a taxing unit can charge up to 20 percent more. Older or disabled homeowners can pay in four installments, the first by February 1.

sections.h2: Which exemptions matter most to San Angelo homeowners?
sections.html:
San Angelo skews older: the Census counts 16.8% of residents at 65 or over and 7,069 veterans, so age and veteran breaks matter. Schools must exempt $140,000 of a homestead, with an extra $60,000 for an owner who is 65-plus or disabled, and cities or counties can stack their own.

  • Once the exemption is in place, a homestead's appraised value is capped at 10 percent growth a year.
  • A school tax freeze holds a senior's school tax at the figure from the year they qualified.
  • Disabled veterans receive $5,000 off at a rating of 10 to 29 percent, rising to $12,000 at 70 percent or higher, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total homestead exemption.

The appraisal district posts a guide to the homestead cap, and applications are due to it by April 30. The Comptroller's exemptions page has the statewide list.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about owning in San Angelo?
sections.html:
Census data show a moderate-cost ownership market in San Angelo. The city has 39,474 households of 2.41 people, with median monthly owner costs of $1,536 on a mortgage and $598 without one. Median rent is $1,153.

  • About 83 percent of residents had not moved in the past year.
  • Owners occupy 61.2 percent of homes.
  • Median household income is $65,864.

These are citywide figures. A written offer or a local agent's pricing opinion will say more about one house than a median does.

sections.h2: How did San Angelo's history shape its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
San Angelo started in the late 1860s as a trading post across the North Concho River from Fort Concho, which opened in 1867. After an 1882 flood destroyed the courthouse at Ben Ficklin, voters chose San Angelo as the new county seat. The Santa Fe railroad reached town in 1888, and the city incorporated in 1903.

Wool, cattle and later oil built the economy. The population doubled from 10,050 in 1920 to 25,308 in 1930, helped by the Permian Basin oil boom. Goodfellow Air Field, picked by the War Department in 1940, brought another surge. The state's historical handbook also credits the city with Angelo State University and a long-established medical sector.

The city now has 100,640 residents, up only 0.7 percent from the 2020 base. It covers 59.70 square miles, and the average commute is 19.2 minutes.

sections.h2: What kind of local economy supports San Angelo home values?
sections.html:
San Angelo sits where the North, South and Middle Concho rivers meet, with farms to the east and ranches to the west, and that mix gave it a broader base than many frontier towns. The state's historical handbook describes the city as the largest sheep market in the United States in its day and lists more than 120 manufacturers.

  • Fort Concho survives as a National Historic Landmark.
  • Goodfellow Air Force Base has offered intelligence training courses to all military branches since 1958.
  • Angelo State University grew out of San Angelo College, founded in 1928.

The Census puts retail sales at $26,742 per person in 2022, and 24.7 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Poverty stands at 11.0 percent.

sections.h2: How are inherited San Angelo homes handled for tax purposes?
sections.html:
An heir who is not named on a recorded deed can still ask the appraisal district for the homestead exemption by supplying an affidavit of ownership interest, the prior owner's death certificate and a recent utility bill. Court record citations may be needed too. Ask the district exactly which papers it wants.

Sort out who may sign a deed before you list. The right route might be probate, a small estate affidavit or an affidavit of heirship, depending on the estate.

sections.h2: What happens to San Angelo taxes at closing?
sections.html:
A claim for each year's tax fastens to the house on January 1, which keeps a buyer from getting clean title while a balance is open. The person who owned it that day stays liable for the year even after selling.

Your closing agent requests the payoff and settles it when the sale funds. The county clerk records the deed, with a $5.00 first-page fee and $4.00 for every added page in the state's manual. Before choosing a closing date, ask the appraisal district for a statement of each unit's balance.

If you are behind on San Angelo tax, a written cash offer can build the payoff into the numbers.

faqs.q: What per-$100 rate does San Angelo list?
faqs.a: The budget page shows $0.7947 per $100 of valuation. Other taxing units add theirs, so the full bill is higher.

faqs.q: Can I pay my San Angelo property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. Look up your account on the Tom Green Central Appraisal District site, open Tax Summary and select the pay link. E-check and cards work.

faqs.q: When must I protest a San Angelo appraisal?
faqs.a: By May 15 or 30 days after delivery of your notice, whichever is later. The district named May 15 for many residential properties, and your notice states your own date.

faqs.q: How high is sales tax in San Angelo?
faqs.a: The total is 8.25 percent: 1 percent for the city, 0.5 for the San Angelo Development Corporation, 0.5 for Tom Green County and 6.25 for the state.

faqs.q: Can I sell a San Angelo house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is settled when the sale funds. Request a written payoff from the Tom Green Central Appraisal District so you know the number in advance.
